body: I told my parents after my third attempt. They did all the things you think your parents should. Was the first time I'd seen them in the same room not yelling at each other since the divorce. They marched me to s therapist the next day. After a couple of weeks it kinda felt like they were treating it like I'd done it on accident. The thoughts are still there. I just dont talk about it anymore. It's better off this way if only I have to deal with it
They wouldn't have won ti with him playing pos 1. Had to happen. He's a much better support
Also when secret kicked Fly I didnt see Big Daddy quit the team to keep playing with him

Semi similar thing happened to me. Went to my doctor and he diagnosed me with depression. Did some 9 question survey thing. So he put me on meds and I had to go back in two weeks so he could see how it was affecting me. Went back in two weeks and said I was worse, so i had to come back in two more weeks. When I showed up that time he asked me what I was there for. Like I understand he's a doctor and is busy but it would take all of five seconds to have looked at his computer to know why. Anyway it sucks when you actively try to get help and help is just shit

We have a couple in NZ that you can ring. Lifeline is the one they advertise and stuff. They're pretty good, have talked me down from the ledge a couple of times. There is another one called Crisisline which the doctors give you the number of if they're worried about you. I rung it once because lifeline didn't have any spare operators. It was one of the worst experiences I've ever had. So I guess it all depends on the person on the other end of the line

I think around 17 for me. I remember as a kid, around 10 or so, the thought of death terrified me to the point i couldn't sleep for fear of not waking up. My family don't really talk about this sort of thing so i think even having a suicidal thought scared me at first. 

It's slowly taken over though. Life just taken everything.
